description: Per-(category, standard) TESTING OBLIGATIONS. Governs which analytes a brand must independently ASSAY per lot, distinct from whether the analyte carries a published LIMIT (every analyte does — HMTc Governing Principles, Certification-Readiness Ruling §1). Authored under the Required-Testing-Panel Ruling (docs/governance/hmtc-governing-principles.md) and operationalized in lot-testing-schedule.md §9. Analyte keys match the compiled standard records exactly (total chromium is 'Cr'; hexavalent is 'Cr-VI'). Validated and fanned to cert by tools/standards/build-required-analytes.mjs.

obligation_vocabulary.per_lot_total: Total-element assay required on every surveillance lot (base ICP-MS panel).
obligation_vocabulary.reflex_speciation: Species assay (iAs/MeHg/Cr-VI) required only when the parent total reaches the reflex trigger; below it the species is bounded by its parent total.
obligation_vocabulary.mandatory_speciation: Species assay required on baseline and every lot regardless of the parent total (defining pathway or materially-present species).
obligation_vocabulary.conditional: Assay required only when a stated, verifiable condition holds (packaging/ingredient).
obligation_vocabulary.baseline_monitor: Assay at the three-lot baseline; not re-tested per lot unless a trigger fires.
obligation_vocabulary.not_applicable: No assay in any lot; the published limit stands as a bounded/read-across ceiling for the record. Never a Tier-1 toxic total.

reflex_trigger_rule: parent-total result >= 50% of the parent-total HMTc limit (lot-testing-schedule.md §9). The Program Operator may lower this per category, never raise it above 50%.

packaging_conditions.metallic_can: tinplate, tin can, or other metal can with direct food contact
packaging_conditions.glass_or_pet: glass or PET bottle (no metallic food-contact surface)

tier_reference.note: Tier follows CLAUDE.md Part 14 / governance-policy.md §2.2. tAs/tHg are the Tier-1 totals that screen the Tier-1 species iAs/MeHg.

olive-oil.summary: The material risks in olive oil are Pb, Ni, and total Cr (not arsenic or mercury). The three speciated tests are all reflex-only: iAs is measured non-detect and bounded by tAs; MeHg has no lipid/marine pathway; Cr-VI reduces to Cr-III in oil. Tin is conditional on metallic packaging. A clean glass-bottled oil therefore runs a single 7-element ICP-MS panel and triggers no speciation.

Pb.rationale: Materially present and the primary regulated risk in olive oil. Frequently detected; typical ~33, p95 66-70, worst individual samples reach the ~100 ug/kg fats-and-oils cap. Tier-1 toxic on the base ICP-MS run.

evidence.pathway: soil uptake; historic leaded-gasoline residue in grove soils; press/milling equipment and brass fittings; ceramic/porcelain packaging

Cd.rationale: Tier-1 toxic; kept on the base ICP-MS run as the litigation shield though the corpus shows it is not material in pressed oil. Cd partitions into the aqueous/press-cake fraction rather than the triacylglycerol lipid; non-detect in the best-controlled study, pool at the ~3 ug/kg analytical floor.

evidence.pathway: minimal in oil — partitions to press-cake

tAs.rationale: Tier-1 toxic and the reflex screen for inorganic arsenic; on the base ICP-MS run. Olive-oil arsenic is trace — typical <1, p95 ~13, often non-detect — far below the 100 ug/kg cap.

iAs.rationale: Bounded by total arsenic (iAs <= tAs). The only speciated olive-oil datum (bodur2023, n=2, HPLC) returned arsenite+arsenate non-detect (LOD 2.86 ug/kg). No lipid arsenic pathway; adjudicated not-material. Speciate only if total As reaches 50 ug/kg (50% of the 100 tAs limit); at typical tAs this never triggers.

tHg.rationale: Tier-1 toxic and the reflex screen for methylmercury; on the base ICP-MS run. Mercury is effectively absent in olive oil (refined-partition); adjudicated not-material.

MeHg.rationale: Bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg). No olive-oil MeHg data exists and there is no marine bioaccumulation pathway for a land-harvested plant oil; methylmercury is physically implausible here. Speciate only if total Hg reaches 10 ug/kg (50% of the 20 tHg limit); at typical tHg this never triggers.

Ni.rationale: MATERIAL — the most likely Tier-2 fail in this category. Frequently detected; typical ~28 but p95 529, p97 577, max 770 ug/kg, driven by refining, bleaching-earth contact, and hydrogenation catalysts (refined/pomace oils). Cold-pressed EVOO clears with headroom (Kabaran 2020 mean 30, max 54). Must be assayed per lot.

evidence.pathway: refining / bleaching earth / hydrogenation catalyst carryover

Al.rationale: MATERIAL and packaging-driven. Detected even in glass (~70-120 baseline), rising ~6-9x in aluminium containers (charfi2026: 670 vs <=120). Cheap on the base ICP-MS run and carries a nonzero baseline, so kept per-lot rather than packaging-conditional. Typical ~246, p95 ~648, below the 1000 limit.

Cr.rationale: Material and the reflex screen for hexavalent chromium; on the base ICP-MS run. Wide right-skewed spread — typical ~98 but p95 613, p97 840, max 945 (best-controlled study only 10-60); high tail from refining. Assayed per lot both as a Tier-2 limit and to gate Cr-VI.

Cr-VI.rationale: Bounded by total Cr and reduces to trivalent chromium in a lipid matrix, so hexavalent Cr is not a standing pathway in oil; no speciated Cr data exists for any oil. Speciate (IC-ICP-MS, EPA 3060A + EPA 6800 / EN 15192) only if total Cr reaches 150 ug/kg (50% of the 300 total-Cr limit); any quantifiable Cr-VI above the 10 ug/kg species ceiling then fails.

evidence.pathway: none in-matrix — Cr(VI) reduces to Cr(III) in lipid

Sn.rationale: No tin pathway in a glass or PET bottle; the only route is migration from tin/tinplate metal packaging (EU 2023/915 canned-food ML is the anchor). Tin is not even measured in the olive-oil corpus (the definitive 32-element packaging scan omitted Sn). Required only for metal-canned/tinplate SKUs; not applicable to glass/PET.

evidence.detection: no data (not measured in olive oil)

cooking-oils-other.summary: Same Cat-30 panel and limits as olive oil. Ni and total Cr are if anything MORE material for refined seed/vegetable oils (canola, sunflower) because refining, bleaching earth, and hydrogenation are more prevalent than in cold-pressed olive oil; both stay per-lot. Speciation reflex-only; tin conditional on metallic packaging.

Pb.rationale: Tier-1 toxic, on the base ICP-MS run; frequently detected across the edible-oil corpus (Pb pool 13 contributing sources). Primary regulated risk.

Cd.rationale: Tier-1 toxic; kept on the base run as the shield. Low in pressed/refined oils (partitions away from the lipid).

tAs.rationale: Tier-1 toxic and reflex screen for iAs; on the base run. Trace in edible oils, far below the 100 cap.

iAs.rationale: Bounded by tAs; no defining arsenic pathway for seed/vegetable oils (no rice). Speciate only if total As reaches 50 ug/kg (50% of 100).

tHg.rationale: Tier-1 toxic and reflex screen for MeHg; on the base run. Effectively absent in plant oils.

MeHg.rationale: Bounded by tHg; no marine pathway for a land-harvested plant oil. Speciate only if total Hg reaches 10 ug/kg (50% of 20).

Ni.rationale: MATERIAL and the most likely Tier-2 fail — refined seed/vegetable oils carry Ni from hydrogenation catalysts and bleaching earth even more than olive oil. Must be assayed per lot.

Al.rationale: Packaging-driven; detected in glass with a baseline, spiking in metal containers. Cheap on the base run; kept per-lot.

Cr.rationale: Material Tier-2 limit and the reflex screen for Cr-VI; on the base run. Wide spread in refined oils from equipment/refining.

Cr-VI.rationale: Bounded by total Cr; reduces to Cr-III in a lipid matrix. Speciate only if total Cr reaches 150 ug/kg (50% of 300).

evidence.pathway: none in-matrix — Cr(VI) to Cr(III) reduction

Sn.rationale: No tin pathway in glass/PET; only migration from tin/tinplate packaging. Not measured in the edible-oil corpus outside a disputed non-olive palm-oil datum. Required only for metal-canned SKUs.
